label: prop:tau-assignment-tower-square
title: The $\tau$-assignment tower square: $H_3 \hookrightarrow H_4$ compatibility
html:
Proposition. The \tau-assignment tower square: H_3 \hookrightarrow H_4 compatibility

Let \iota_{34} denote the inclusion of the H_3 normal-form module into the H_4 normal-form module by extension with zero, the 24-element basis being ordered with the H_3 basis as its prefix. At the monodromy point q = i write N_n = \sigma - i for the Jordan nilpotent of the generator action on the rank-n module. Then the tower data commute at every level:

  1. action: \iota_{34} intertwines the generator actions on the two modules;
  2. nilpotent: \iota_{34} \circ N_3 = N_4 \circ \iota_{34};
  3. trace: the rank-4 Markov trace restricts along \iota_{34} to the rank-3 Markov trace;
  4. assignment: the rank-4 \tau-assignment onto the genus-4 H^{1,0} model restricts along \iota_{34} to the rank-3 assignment, and likewise for the conjugate H^{0,1} partner;
  5. surjectivity: the image of either assignment is the full three-dimensional isotypic slot of H^{1,0}, with witnesses at rank 4 obtained by pushing rank-3 witnesses forward along \iota_{34}.

Moreover the square itself is not special to these two rungs. For any Coxeter system and any generator subset J, extension by zero along the parabolic coset decomposition intertwines both the generator actions and the q = i nilpotents, with no hypothesis beyond subgroup membership; and for any marked pair s_i, s_j with m_{ij} = 3 and s_i \neq s_j, an assignment with all four laws exists on the full group at every rank and on every parabolic containing the pair, factoring through the base-rung assignment by restriction to the six-element cell, with the corresponding restriction square commuting. Kernel exactness — the identification of the semisimple quotient with the isotypic slot — holds at the base rung n = 3; at higher rungs the assignment factors through a larger semisimple quotient without being injective on it. Strict pair-independence fails: at the A_3 rung the assignments for the two braid pairs are provably different functions, the indicator state of the longest cell element of one pair being read into the isotypic slot by that pair's assignment and annihilated by the other's. Coherence between distinct pairs holds along two proved edge classes: any symmetry of the Coxeter matrix, and any conjugation carrying one marked pair onto another, each inducing a group endomorphism along which the target pair's assignment is the pullback of the source pair's. The pair swap (s_i, s_j) \mapsto (s_j, s_i) is the proved exception: it transports the six-element cell by an index involution, but no map on the isotypic target — linear or otherwise — completes its square. The coherent edges assemble: on the category of marked pairs, with morphisms the group homomorphisms carrying one marking to the other, the assignment family is a natural transformation from the contravariant state functor to the constant isotypic functor, and both proved edge classes are isomorphisms, so the transformation restricts to the core groupoid of marked pairs. This is the correct sense in which the pair-dependent family is canonical: not a single pair-independent map — that is refuted — but a coherently indexed one. The two coherence directions compose — a groupoid edge between pairs inside a common parabolic pastes with the restriction square — and the Markov trace of the cell restriction is intertwined by every edge, so trace values are well-defined on marked-pair orbits and may be quoted without naming the pair.
